title: KiroCrew official app registry
description: Curated app catalog. Answers exactly two questions per app: WHAT it is (identity) and WHERE its bytes come from (source). Everything else is either GENERATED at publish time from the app's own app.json, or belongs in editorial.json (presentation) -- never hand-authored here. This document must not name other registries (catalog sources come from owner config or the build-time edition seam), must not carry presentation (that is editorial.json), and must not carry executable strings (the client never runs a command supplied by a fetched document).

schemaVersion.description: Integer major. A major this client does not support triggers full fallback, not a partial read.

generatedAt.description: Publish stamp. Set by CI, not by curators.

revision.description: Opaque publish revision id. Published payloads are immutable per revision -- never rewrite one with different bytes.

apps.description: Capped only as a sanity bound; the real defense against an oversized document is a transfer-size limit in the client, since a schema limit is only reached after the whole payload has been parsed. Note `removed`/`reinstated` are deliberately NOT capped: they are append-only history, and a schema limit that truncated them would start resurrecting withdrawn apps.

removed.description: Tombstones. Positive removal data that outranks a stale cached entry.

reinstated.description: Explicit reinstatement records. The ONLY thing that may clear a persisted tombstone -- omission from `removed` must never resurrect an app. Permanently append-only, never pruned.

appName.description: Unique app id. Same gate as the runtime KEBAB_RE in apps/manifest.py -- a traversing or absolute name must never reach a filesystem path.

entry.description: AUTHORED: name + source. GENERATED at publish from the app's app.json: everything below the divider. A curator never types the generated fields, and an app author never edits this document.

summary.description: Short, list-safe. Long-form body/screenshots/highlights are never baked -- they stay lazy on the detail view.

categories.description: Curator-assigned membership, carried through from the authored catalog. ORDER IS MEANINGFUL: the first entry is the primary category and is the one that places the app in a rail; a second only widens search and filtering. A client that does not recognise an id must SKIP it rather than reject the document, so an added category does not break older clients.

tags.description: AUTHOR-DECLARED, free-form, and VISIBLE as filter facets. Not a place for search synonyms -- use searchAliases for those.

searchAliases.description: Invisible search synonyms ("deck", "powerpoint"). Matched by search, never rendered as chips -- which is why these are not tags.

iconRef.description: Path to the app's icon, never a URL. A builtin names an absolute client-local path (/app-assets/<app>/icon.svg) whose bytes it already ships; every other source names a repo-relative path the client rewrites onto its own proxy. Honouring an absolute location from a fetched manifest would put a publisher-chosen host into a document we sign.

iconRefDark.description: Optional dark-appearance variant of iconRef, same shape rules. Raster art has fixed bytes, so an app that must read well on both backgrounds ships two files; a builtin's inline SVG repaints from theme tokens and needs none.

categoryId.description: A category id, as declared in editorial.json. Deliberately not an enum here: the taxonomy lives in one document, and copying it into this schema would be a second source of truth that drifts. Existence is checked cross-document at publish.

author.description: Structured from the start: a bare string cannot carry a link or distinguish a person from an org, and widening string -> object later would be a breaking change. The publish step normalizes a legacy bare string into { name }.

source.description: Where the app's BYTES come from. Closed discriminated union: exactly one variant, no extra properties, and each variant's pinning field is required. A loosely-modelled source would validate an archive with no digest -- an unpinned download.

sourceBuiltin.title: builtin -- resolved from the client's own inventory
sourceBuiltin.description: An app bundled in the KiroCrew release the user already installed. There is deliberately NOTHING to fetch here and no digest: integrity comes from the signed application bundle, so a url or hash would be a second, weaker claim about bytes this document does not deliver. Additional properties are closed, which makes an entry carrying a clone target unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. IMPORTANT for clients: this is a CLAIM in a fetched document, not an authorization. Resolve a built-in from your own inventory and never let a catalog entry designate one, or an entry naming an app you ship could shadow or impersonate it.

minClientVersion.description: The earliest KiroCrew release carrying this app, when known. A client older than this can still LIST the app and tell the user to update, which is the point: the shelf stops being pinned to the client's release cadence. Full semver, because prereleases (0.2.0-nightly.20260806t065257, 0.2.0-rc.1) are real shipping versions; anchored at both ends, because an unanchored pattern accepts a trailing payload that then renders in a signed document.

sourceGit.title: git (the only variant implemented in v1)

url.description: https only, because a git URL is an execution vector once it reaches `git clone`: the `ext::` transport runs a command, a value beginning with `-` is argument injection into the git invocation, and `file://` reads arbitrary local paths. Restricting the scheme here keeps this document consistent with its own rule against carrying executable strings, rather than deferring entirely to a trusted-host gate that lives in the client and does not exist yet. This also costs nothing in practice: no trust tier supplies ambient clone credentials, so an ssh URL could not authenticate anyway. Self-hosted forges are still fine -- any https host works, and WHICH hosts may be cloned remains a separate allowlist gate.

ref.description: MUST be a full immutable commit id. A branch name is a mutable pointer, so a signed index naming `main` signs nothing about the bytes. The publish pipeline resolves the curator's branch/tag to a commit and emits that.

subdir.description: Contained relative path: no absolute, no '..', no backslash, no NUL, and not empty (omit the field instead of passing ""). The '..' rule is a substring test, so it also rejects otherwise-legitimate names containing a double dot such as 'a..b'. That is deliberate -- this value becomes a filesystem path, and a conservative test is worth more than the rare directory name it costs.

sourceS3.title: s3 (reserved)
sourceS3.description: Separate from `archive` because the auth model differs: SigV4 with a region and an explicit credential grant vs an anonymous HTTPS GET. Needing credentials at all makes this variant contingent on the per-repository credential-grant mechanism -- no trust tier ever supplies them.

sourceBundle.title: bundle (reserved)
sourceBundle.description: Prebuilt ESM bundle. Maps the federated-app-platform RFC's bundleUrl + bundleHash onto this union.

advice.description: What the client should do about an ALREADY-INSTALLED copy. Default 'keep' -- only a yank escalates to 'uninstall'.
